correctness.rationale: For finite rooted trees, all subtree leaf-query sets are laminar. A query vertex cannot occur twice in a full shattered tree: repetition along a path is constant, and laminarity makes it constant on one side of the least common ancestor for incomparable uses. The \(2^{d-1}-1\) query nodes above the last level are distinct nonroot nonleaf tree vertices; adding the root gives \(I\ge2^{d-1}\), and distinct leaf hypotheses require \(L\ge2^d\). Two-copy grafting constructs T_d with exact equality and a complete depth-d shattered tree; adding root leaves and subdividing edges reaches all I,L. Exhaustive exact game enumeration through twelve vertices and explicit complete certificates through depth five verified the constructions. The single-vertex/one-leaf boundary has dimension zero.

evidence: Walker Theorems 1.3 and 1.17 concern counts and embedding ranks of leaf subsets in uniform binary trees; Section 1.1 derives general Sauer-type shatter-function inequalities. Chase–Freitag–Reyzin derive expected query learning and compression results for general classes, not tree-vertex extremizers. Ghazi et al. establish aggregation closure bounds.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The information bound from L distinct hypotheses yields only \(L\ge2^d\); generic closure/compression theorems do not imply the additional sharp \(I\ge2^{d-1}\). Walker has related words leaf/tree/dimension but a different definition, and its fixed ambient full binary tree is not the arbitrary vertex-minimization problem.

originality.rationale: Specific all-depth bivariate extremal law for dual leaf-path concepts. Walkers 2022 binary-leaf tree dimension embeds a tree into a branch poset; it is not the adaptive membership-query dimension for all rooted trees and does not imply the sharp leaf/nonleaf count. General online dimension, closure and query learning papers are broader in subject but lack this shape-resource bound in their examined material. Related historical descendant-cone work uses the opposite incidence orientation and all vertices as hypotheses, so its height bounds do not cover the minimal size or bicriteria formula. No equivalent or dominating result was found in actual semantic and primary searches. Priority beyond those sources is a residual risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed or inaccessible specialized literature on laminar query systems may contain an equivalent sharp minimum-size theorem.

value.rationale: The exact bivariate maximum resolves a natural hierarchical learning capacity as a function of both hypothesis count (leaves) and available adaptive membership-query structure (nonleaf vertices), not an arbitrary finite slice. It gives a sharp all-depth smallest witness \(3\cdot2^{d-1}\) and exact order-n maximum while every such class has VC dimension at most one. The extra I bound is a structural laminar limitation absent from the trivial \(2^d\) hypothesis bound; it applies to any size and admits explicit optimal constructions.
